title: Populate per-session MCP allowlist before tool injection (scope actually trims the surface)
author: coding-agent
summary: ws_gateway.handleInputFrame's per-turn PATCH to the fork session (the #765 'push the resolved MCP allowlist onto the existing fork session' block) derived the pushed `servers` list by JSON.parsing wsMcpRoleConfig.allowedToolsJson and casting it `as string[]`. That field is the RAW, UNEXPANDED profile allowed_mcps_json column value, which — per agent_profile_scope.ts _buildMcpRoleConfig — can be EITHER a bare server-name array (`["canva","obsidian"]`, parses fine) OR a tools-map object (`{"canva":["tool1"],"obsidian":[...]}`, parses to a plain object). When a profile's allowed_mcps_json is stored in tools-map form, the cast lied: `updateSessionAllowlist` sent `{ mcpAllowlist: { servers: <object>, tools: [] } }` to the fork's PATCH /session/:id endpoint. The fork's Session.McpAllowlist schema declares `servers: Schema.Array(Schema.String)` — Effect Schema rejects an object where an array is required, the PATCH fails, and ws_gateway's wrapping try/catch swallows the failure as 'non-fatal'. The session's mcpAllowlist is left undefined on the fork, so prompt.ts's filterMcpToolsByAllowlist takes the `undefined` branch (all tools pass) and injects the FULL ~150K tool surface for every profiled turn on that code path — reproducing the confirmed Gemini 400 function_declaration-exceeds symptom even though the ws_gateway log correctly reported the resolved profile and its servers.

diagnosis.which: (a) + (c) combined — not (b). The PATCH IS awaited before promptFn is dispatched (no race), but the guard `if (wsMcpRoleConfig?.allowedToolsJson)` only checks presence/truthiness, and the value it gates on (`allowedToolsJson`) is the wrong, unexpanded field: it is the raw profile JSON string (array OR tools-map shape) rather than the already-tested, schema-matching {servers[], tools[]} shape that createSession's expandMcpAllowlist() produces for the exact same McpRoleConfig type.
diagnosis.confirmed_by: apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts line ~211-214 (McpAllowlist = Schema.Struct({ servers: Schema.mutable(Schema.Array(Schema.String)), tools: ... })); apps/api_server/src/controllers/agent_sessions_controller.ts line ~476-487 (mcpAllowedToolsJson is built as JSON.stringify(Record<string,string[]>) — an OBJECT — whenever a session is created via an .mcp-roles/<slug>.mcp.json role file, which is the per-tool-scoped shape graphic-designer's canva/obsidian restriction requires); apps/api_server/src/services/agent_profile_scope.ts `_buildMcpRoleConfig` (accepts + passes through BOTH array and tools-map JSON forms as allowedToolsJson unchanged).

constraints.fix_location: api_server-side only (ws_gateway.ts call site + opencode_client_service.updateSessionAllowlist signature) — no fork change needed; the fork's schema/filter logic was already correct and unit-tested
constraints.single_choke_point: updateSessionAllowlist now takes the whole McpRoleConfig and calls the SAME expandMcpAllowlist() helper createSession already uses, so the PATCH path and the init-time create path can never diverge in shape again
constraints.dispatch_enforcement_unchanged: #765/#775 dispatch enforcement (mcp_dispatch_guard) untouched — this fix only corrects what shape is PATCHed to the fork session, not the dispatch-time guard

acceptance_tests.description: updateSessionAllowlist(sessionId, mcpRoleConfig) PATCHes body.mcpAllowlist deep-equal to expandMcpAllowlist(mcpRoleConfig) — correct shape for a tools-map-form profile (e.g. graphic-designer: canva with explicit allowedTools)
acceptance_tests.assertion: capturedBody.mcpAllowlist.servers and .tools are both string[] (never an object) and deep-equal expandMcpAllowlist(roleConfig)

acceptance_tests.description: updateSessionAllowlist correctly expands a bare-array-form profile too (back-compat with the simple designer-UI server-toggle case)
acceptance_tests.assertion: servers[] contains inherit-all server names; tools[] empty for those servers

acceptance_tests.description: ws_gateway pushes the allowlist for EVERY profiled turn (guard keys on wsMcpRoleConfig presence, not on the now-removed allowedToolsJson shape check) — falsifiable: reverting the guard to check allowedToolsJson truthiness must not un-falsify this, since allowedToolsJson is always truthy when mcpRoleConfig is non-null (this AC targets the shape bug, not the presence guard)
acceptance_tests.assertion: opencodeClient.updateSessionAllowlist is called once per handleInputFrame invocation with the exact wsMcpRoleConfig object when a profile resolves

acceptance_tests.description: Unprofiled session (no mcpRoleConfig resolved) — back-compat: updateSessionAllowlist is NOT called at all, leaving the fork session's allowlist untouched (unrestricted)
acceptance_tests.assertion: opencodeClient.updateSessionAllowlist is not called when resolveProfileScope returns mcpRoleConfig: null

acceptance_tests.description: Falsification: a tools-map-shaped allowedToolsJson previously produced a non-array `servers` field on the PATCH body (reproducing the pre-fix bug) — this test fails against the OLD code and passes against the NEW code
acceptance_tests.assertion: Array.isArray(capturedBody.mcpAllowlist.servers) === true for a ROLE_CONFIG built from a tools-map-form allowedToolsJson

ws_gateway_per_turn_patch.before: if (wsMcpRoleConfig?.allowedToolsJson) { const servers = JSON.parse(wsMcpRoleConfig.allowedToolsJson) as string[]; await opencodeClient.updateSessionAllowlist(opencodeId, servers); }

update_session_allowlist.before: async updateSessionAllowlist(sessionId: string, servers: string[]): body = { mcpAllowlist: { servers, tools: [] } }
update_session_allowlist.after: async updateSessionAllowlist(sessionId: string, mcpRoleConfig: McpRoleConfig): body = { mcpAllowlist: expandMcpAllowlist(mcpRoleConfig) }

not_in_scope.fork_changes: none required — apps/opencode_fork/packages/opencode/src/session/{prompt.ts,mcp_allowlist.ts,session.ts} were already correct; this is purely an api_server-side wrong-shape-push bug
not_in_scope.real_binary_smoke: NOT required for this fix, since no fork code changed — the fix corrects the JSON shape sent to an ALREADY-CORRECT, already-shipped fork schema/filter. Standard `npx vitest run` + `tsc --noEmit` on api_server is sufficient evidence. (If a future issue touches the fork itself, that would need a real-binary smoke per AGENTS.md.)

validation_commands: cd apps/api_server && npx vitest run ws_gateway mcp_allowlist mcp_dispatch_guard opencode_client
